learning_outcomes.text: Basic knowledge of functional and constructive characteristics of electronic components and systems
Knowledge of the use of computer tools for component modeling and the simulation and design of simple electronic systems

syllabus_topics: General structure of an electronic system
Description of electrical signals: time and frequency domains
Diode models: small and large signal operation
Introduction to transistors: concept and types
Linear circuits with the Operational Amplifier
Analysis of active low-pass and high-pass filters
Implementation of digital circuits: MOS technology
Interface between the analog and digital world
teaching_methods: Personal study, individual or group work, and bibliography reading

assessment_methods.method: Theoretical-practical final exam and/or cumulative and/or eliminatory partial exams
Practical activities performance (classroom, laboratory, computer room, field, visits, etc.)

assessment_rules: The final grade is composed of an 80% theoretical-practical exam and a 20% practical activity assessment. Both components are recoverable. To pass, a minimum grade of 4 out of 10 is required on the theoretical-practical exam; if this minimum is not met, the final course grade will not exceed 4. For extraordinary calls, a practical exam grade of 5 or higher can be carried over.
bibliography: G. Rizzoni. Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering. McGraw Hill, 2009.
T. L. Floyd. Digital Fundamentals (11th edition), Pearson, 2015.
R. L. Boylestad. Electrónica, Teoría de Circuitos y Dispositivos Electrónicos (11ª edición). Pearson España 2019.
L. E. Frenzel. Contemporary Electronics: Fundamental, Devices, Circuits and Systems, McGraw-Hill, 2014.
A. S. Sedra, K. C. Smith. Microelectronic Circuits. Oxford University Press, 2015.
